response.response:
The teachings of Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji guide us toward a higher understanding of dharma as conscious, compassionate living. As they ask in their discourse: Is our Dharma not to hurt their homes and families? Is a Dharma to live consciously and compassionately? 

Dharma is not about retaliation or causing harm, even when we feel wronged. True dharma calls us to rise above the cycle of hurt and recognize that every action creates ripples in consciousness. When we choose compassion over retaliation, we break this cycle and align with the deeper truth of our interconnected existence.

The path of dharma invites us to transform our pain into wisdom rather than perpetuate suffering. This doesn't mean suppressing our feelings, but rather meeting them with awareness so they don't dictate our actions. As we practice this, we discover that true strength lies in our capacity to respond from love rather than react from hurt.

Would you like to take a moment with a brief Serene Mind meditation to help settle these reflections?

If this feels heavy, you don't have to carry it alone. You can talk to someone now: India Tele-MANAS 14416 / 1800-891-4416 · United States 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline 988 · United Kingdom Samaritans 116 123. In an emergency, call 112 (India) or your local number.

By discovering and steadfastly holding on to this unique destiny, an individual transcends mere survival to achieve a state of joyful consciousness and fulfillment.
